fabric-api-base.reason: Shipped by Fabricated (vendored from upstream); every Fabric API module builds on it. Its package net.fabricmc.fabric.api.util is split with fabric-content-registries-v0, whose two interfaces there (Block2ObjectMap, Item2ObjectMap) Fabricated ships with it, as the in-game mod's packages are taken out of Fabric jars.

fabric-dimensions-v1.reason: Forge loads DataFixerUpper outside the layers Mixin transforms, so upstream's TaggedChoiceMixin and TaggedChoiceTypeMixin would never apply (pre-flight disabled the module for them), and Schema2832Mixin, which casts DataFixerUpper's tagged choice type to the interface they add, would fail when the data fixers are built: the three are left out and the rest of the module loads, as on Forge 61 to 66. Nothing is lost: Forge 52 patches the same schema (V2832) to keep a dimension's generator as it is when its type isn't known (DSL.or with DSL.remainder()), which is what upstream's mixins are for (read in Forge 52.1.21).

fabric-entity-events-v1.reason: Forge's LivingEntity asks the bed's state (BlockState.setBedOccupied, getBedDirection) where vanilla sets the occupied property and asks BedBlock, which upstream's occupation and sleeping direction hooks look for: Fabricated's in-game mod runs SET_BED_OCCUPATION_STATE and MODIFY_SLEEPING_DIRECTION at Forge's calls and sets the occupied state of the block that is there (SLEEP-1, as on Forge 47 and 61 to 66). Upstream's sleep time hooks redirect Level.isDay() as a player tries to sleep and as a sleeping one ticks, where Forge 52 checks its SleepingTimeCheckEvent instead (falling back to that check): the in-game mod answers Forge's event from Fabric's ALLOW_SLEEP_TIME, with vanilla's answer, when no Forge mod has (SLEEP-2, as on Forge 47).

fabric-events-interaction-v0.reason: Forge's destroyBlock no longer calls Block.playerWillDestroy and Block.destroy itself, where upstream's hooks fire PlayerBlockBreakEvents.BEFORE and AFTER: both moved into a private removeBlock Forge added. Fabricated's in-game mod fires them at the same points of Forge's method instead, BEFORE (with CANCELED when refused) once the game's checks pass and AFTER once removeBlock removed the block, before the drops (BREAK-1, as on Forge 47 and 61 to 66).

fabric-key-binding-api-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated: upstream's API, its key bindings registered on Forge's key mapping event, where Forge mods register theirs. Upstream refuses a key binding once the game's options exist, and Forge 52 creates them before it loads mods, the Fabric client entrypoints among them, so passed through, the module would fail every client entrypoint that registers one (KEYMAP-3, as on Forge 47 and 61 to 66). Forge loads the keys from the options file again once mods have loaded, which gives each key binding the key the player saved. As upstream, a key binding registered twice is refused, and so is one registered once Forge's event has added them; a category new to the game is sorted after the game's, by upstream's accessor of the categories' order; KeyBindingHelper.getBoundKeyOf reads the key binding's key through upstream's accessor.

fabric-loot-api-v3.reason: Shipped by Fabricated: upstream's builder and accessor mixins as they are; its loading hooks are replaced by Forge's LootTableLoadEvent (REPLACE and MODIFY, once per table) and Fabricated's hook on the reload of the reloadable registries (ALL_LOADED), as on Forge 61 to 65. A table's source is decided from the id of the pack its file comes from (mods' data is a pack per mod file on Forge), where upstream reads fabric-resource-loader-v0's pack sources.

fabric-tag-api-v1.reason: Forge's tag files already have a remove list, which its tag loader applies, and upstream's FabricTagFile.remove() reads it: upstream's own list conflicts with Forge's (pre-flight disabled the module: TagFile.remove() exists already), and its tag loader hooks, which apply that list, are left out with it. Fabricated adds fabric:remove entries to Forge's list instead (the in-game mod's TagFileRemoveMixin), as on Forge 61 to 66.

fabric-particles-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated: upstream's API, its hook that registers Fabric's particle factories once the engine's own are in, the accessors its sprite provider reads, and its block dust tint event, asked where Forge 52 decides the tint (its block extensions' areBreakingParticlesTinted replaced vanilla's grass check, which upstream's hook looks for). Forge 52 keeps the particle engine's factories in a map by the type's id, which upstream's accessor reads as a map by raw id: Fabric's factories and their sprite sets are registered through the engine's own methods, where Forge registers its mods' (PART-1, as on Forge 47).
